sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: An amulet is an object worn or carried to keep off harm. The Celts used amulets from the earliest times. An amulet is not the same as a talisman. A talisman draws good luck, or the blessing of the gods, to its owner. An amulet drives off evil spirits and bad luck. Early Celtic magic carried two aims. It kept bad events away, and it drew good things near. An amulet served the first aim. Archaeologists have found apparent amulets at the early Celtic sites of La Tène and Hallstatt. For the most famous Celtic amulet, see Serpent Stone.
